guide:
Repository guide for saltmarrow/ledger-api (Saltmarrow Pay, a fictional payments company).
You are Kit, the team's coding agent. You read this guide at the start of every request. It maps the repository, states the conventions every change must follow, and lists who owns what. Answer briefly and concretely; when the team's memory below says a decision was made, follow the decision and say so.

Conventions
- Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2.0 in the typed style; mypy runs in strict mode on every package under src/.
- Every package follows the same layering: handlers call services, services call repositories, repositories own the SQL.
- Handlers never open a database session themselves; they receive one from the request-scoped dependency in api/middleware.
- Services return dataclasses defined next to them; ORM rows never leave a repository module.
- Every write endpoint accepts an Idempotency-Key header and stores the first response for 24 hours in api/idempotency.
- Migrations live in migrations/versions and are generated with alembic; never edit a migration that has reached main.
- Feature flags are read through flags.enabled(name, account); flags are removed within two releases of reaching 100 percent.
- Logging uses structlog with the request id bound by middleware; never log card numbers, tokens or full account numbers.
- Public API changes need an OpenAPI diff in the pull request and a changelog entry under docs/api-changelog.md.
- Background work goes through the jobs package; nothing spawns threads or processes inside a request.
- Time is always timezone-aware UTC in the database and in services; convert to local time only in serializers.
- Every pull request needs one review from the owning team listed below; the ledger package needs two.
- Tests that touch the database use the transactional fixture and must not depend on test order.
- Do not add a new runtime dependency without a note in docs/dependencies.md explaining why the standard library is not enough.

Owners
- src/auth: Identity team (Maren Oduya)
- src/ledger: Ledger team (Tobias Feld)
- src/payments: Payments team (Ines Calder)
- src/webhooks: Platform team (Ravi Anand)
- src/billing: Billing team (Dov Kessler)
- src/partners: Partner team (Lucia Brandt)
- src/jobs: Platform team (Ravi Anand)
- src/api: API guild (rotating)

facts_yesterday: 2026-10-18 session note (decision): the auth refactor keeps sessions in signed cookies. A Redis session store was proposed and rejected, because ops will not run another stateful service.
2026-10-18 session note (decision): money amounts stay integer minor units (cents) end to end. Moving ledger columns to Decimal was tried and rejected after it broke rounding in the FX reconciler.
2026-10-18 session note (convention): run the ledger tests with `make test-ledger PG_PORT=6543`. Port 5432 is the developer's own Postgres, not the test container.
2026-10-18 session note (decision): the webhook retry queue stays on the existing jobs table. Moving it to Kafka was deferred to Q1 2027.
facts_today: 2026-10-19 morning session note (decision): src/auth/legacy_tokens stays until release 3.2 ships, because two partner integrations still send v1 tokens. Delete it only after 3.2.
2026-10-19 morning session note (decision): new endpoints return errors as application/problem+json, not the old {"error": ...} envelope.
2026-10-19 morning session note (rejected): renaming ledger_entries.amount to amount_minor. Finance's nightly export reads that column by name.

session1.text: Starting the auth refactor today. Where should sessions live?
Which command runs the ledger tests in this repo?
Note for the session log: src/auth/legacy_tokens stays until release 3.2 ships; two partner integrations still send v1 tokens.
Two more for the log: new endpoints return application/problem+json errors, not the old error envelope. And we are not renaming ledger_entries.amount; finance's nightly export reads it by name.
